newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farmers shake off BSE effect on beef sector.
newsitem.headline: German farmers shake off BSE effect on beef sector.

text.p: German farmers are beginning to overcome the worst effects of a beef demand slump in connection with the so-called mad cow disease, farm union DBV said on Tuesday.
"Initiatives to re-establish trust in beef and EU measures...have helped us master the crisis," DBV leader Constantin Freiherr Heereman said in remarks prepared for delivery at a press conference.
Farmers hurt by the scare over bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) had benefited from EU intervention buying and third country exports, he said.
Of the 420,000 tonnes of beef currently in intervention, some 120,000 tonnes were German supplies.
The crisis was arose after the British government admitted in March BSE might be transmitted to humans.
Heereman said German beef consumption slumped by up to 40 percent in the wake of the announcement but had since recovered to a level three percent below that seen a year ago.

Producer prices of young bulls had recaptured year-ago levels of 5.20 marks per kilo slaughter weight but heifer prices were still 0.50 marks/kg down and those of slaughter cows down 0.30 marks from prices seen 12 months ago.
Heereman pegged total lost income from lower prices achieved by farmers' 4.25 million beef slaughterings this year at 750 million marks.
